newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris not negotiating settlements.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris not negotiating settlements.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said it was not negotiating with anyone, including plaintiffs' lawyers or any state attorney general, regarding the settlement of tobacco litigation.
The company said in a statement: "As far as we can tell, the attorneys general are negotiating with themselves."

Fourteen states are seeking reimbursement for Medicaid funds spent on smoking-related illnesses, most in suits that seek $1 billion or more. Philip Morris has also been hit by subpoenas from the Justice Department as part of a fraud investigation.
The Wall Street Journal has reported legislation intended to create a broad settlement of most of the lawsuits was circulating in Congress.

The statement said in part, "The states and their private contingent-fee lawyers obviously do not believe that Medicaid reimbursement cases have merit and therefore in an act of desperation are attempting to get money for themselves through the legislation route.
"These cases are indeed without merit and we believe all of them eventually should be dismissed by the courts as the law requires. In the meantime, we are preparing for trials."
